style.vernacular: Soviet-planned Central Asian capital on the Varzob river: tree-lined boulevards (Rudaki Avenue) of 3-6 storey pastel-stucco neoclassical and late-Soviet panel blocks, grand columned public buildings in cream and white, newer white-marble and glass state buildings with Persian/Samanid motifs and blue-tiled domes, low courtyard houses with flat or low-pitched metal roofs on the outskirts, and plane, poplar and mulberry shade trees everywhere.
style.ornament: Persian/Samanid revival: pointed iwan arches, ganch (carved plaster) panels, turquoise and blue glazed tile domes, geometric girih bands; Soviet monumental columned porticoes, relief friezes and state emblems on civic blocks; national flag on a 165 m pole; golden Samanid crown motif.

sources.what: Csa Mediterranean climate; Rudaki Avenue, Palace of the Nation, Supreme Soviet and National Library buildings; 22% green space with introduced tree species
new parliament on Rudaki Avenue: white marble facade, 70 m dome, Tajik styling
vernacular Central Asian courtyard mosque with L-shaped columned porticoes, semicircular-arched gatehouse and carved-wood screens
